name: Workforce Management
description: Planning and control loop for agent supply: contact-volume forecasting, schedule generation, intraday adherence management, and shrinkage accounting that together determine whether service levels are staffable.
roleInCenter: Supply-side brain: predict demand and place agent hours where the ACD will need them.

glossary.definition: Predicted contact volume and AHT per interval, feeding staffing requirements
Planning time slice, typically 15 or 30 minutes
Agents needed per interval after occupancy, shrinkage, and SL targets applied
Share of paid time agents are not available to handle contacts
Assigned shifts, breaks, and activities per agent per week
Share of scheduled on-queue time the agent was actually available
Schedule worked vs contracted hours regardless of timing; adherence is about timing
Share of available agent time spent handling/wrapping contacts; burnout risk above ~85-90%
Same-day rebalancing: moving aux time, lunches, or extra queues as actuals diverge from forecast
Queueing model converting volume, AHT, and SL target into agent count
Window before a schedule week when trades and time-off close so staffing is stable
Seniority or performance-based process for assigning recurring schedules

metrics.name: Forecast Accuracy
metrics.definition: 100 minus interval MAPE between forecast and actual volume

metrics.name: Schedule Adherence
metrics.definition: Time in adherence over scheduled on-queue time

metrics.name: Shrinkage
metrics.definition: Unavailable share of paid agent time, planned + unplanned

metrics.name: Occupancy
metrics.definition: Handling+ACW share of available time; sustained >90% is burnout exposure

metrics.name: Staffing Variance
metrics.definition: Requirement minus staffed per interval; negative means SL at risk

metrics.name: Actual AHT per Interval
metrics.definition: Handle+hold+ACW mean used by forecast; a leading driver, not just an outcome

failureModes.name: Forecast Blind Spots
failureModes.signal: Campaign or outage volume arrives unbudgeted; interval requirement understated
failureModes.mitigation: Outbound and notification calendars wired into forecast inputs

failureModes.name: Shrinkage Undercount
failureModes.signal: Planned schedule never achieves SL because shrinkage factor below actual
failureModes.mitigation: Recalculate monthly from aux actuals; separate planned vs unplanned trend lines

failureModes.name: Adherence Whack-a-Mole
failureModes.signal: Intraday moves cascade breaks into coverage gaps later in day
failureModes.mitigation: Move-in-time budgets; escalate to supervisor only past concurrency threshold

failureModes.name: Occupancy Burnout
failureModes.signal: Occupancy >90% with rising absenteeism and QA soft-skill scores falling
failureModes.mitigation: Surge staffing plan, attrition-risk review, aux recovery windows

exchanges: Interval stats (volume, SL, ASA) as forecast actuals
Aux codes used for adherence state matching
Coaching blocks scheduled as planned shrinkage
Campaign calendars as forecast input events
Schedule satisfaction items in employee pulse instruments

scoringModel.name: WFM Intraday Forecasting & Occupancy Health Scorecard
scoringModel.note: Evaluates interval arrival forecasting accuracy, shrinkage accounting fidelity, real-time adherence governance, and burnout-safe occupancy bands.

dimensions.name: Interval Arrival & AHT Forecast Precision
dimensions.description: Accuracy of 15-minute and 30-minute volume and AHT predictions incorporating seasonal baselines and outbound event overlays
sampleCriteria: Interval volume MAPE stays below 7 percent across prime hours
AHT forecast variance stays within 10 percent of interval actuals
Marketing and outbound calendars ingested prior to schedule lock

dimensions.name: Shrinkage Calibration & Real-Time Adherence
dimensions.description: Alignment between budgeted and observed planned and unplanned shrinkage paired with schedule adherence discipline
sampleCriteria: Real-time schedule adherence exceeds 90 percent across skilled queues
Planned versus actual shrinkage variance stays under 2.5 percentage points
Aux state codes map cleanly between ACD telemetry and WFM rosters

dimensions.name: Occupancy Health & Burnout Equilibrium
dimensions.description: Maintenance of productive occupancy inside the sustainable 78 to 86 percent band without inducing agent fatigue spirals
sampleCriteria: Interval occupancy remains within 78 to 86 percent target corridor
Zero teams sustain occupancy above 90 percent for 4+ consecutive intervals
Coaching and recovery aux blocks protected from routine cancellation

dimensions.name: Intraday Surplus & Deficit Rebalancing Agility
dimensions.description: Speed and stability of intraday flex actions when live arrival intensity diverges from tactical schedule plans
sampleCriteria: Intraday flex or skill-rebalance triggers within 15 minutes of 2-sigma volume spike
Break adjustments preserve downstream afternoon coverage without cascade gaps
Net staffing variance stays within plus or minus 5 percent of Erlang requirement

dimensions.name: Schedule Ergonomics & Shift Conformance
dimensions.description: Fairness of shift bids, adherence to freeze windows, and full conformance to labor and break regulations
sampleCriteria: Schedule published ahead of freeze window with zero labor rule violations
Shift conformance sits between 98 and 102 percent of contracted hours
Employee pulse schedule satisfaction trends positive quarter over quarter

stateVariables.description: Continuous intraday arrival intensity driven by an inhomogeneous Poisson baseline plus self-exciting Hawkes outage and retry bursts
Instantaneous fraction of scheduled paid agent capacity unavailable due to planned and unplanned shrinkage diffusion
Accumulated cognitive and physiological agent fatigue state driven by sustained high occupancy above the recovery threshold
Continuous net staffing balance equal to effective available agents minus instantaneous Erlang-A required staffing
Intraday management control flow reallocating aux windows, cross-skilled pools, and overtime to damp staffing deficits

differentialEquations.name: Inhomogeneous Poisson-Hawkes Intraday Arrival Intensity
differentialEquations.formula: dlambda(t) = kappa_lam cdot (lambda_base(t) - lambda(t)) dt + alpha_hawk cdot dN_retry(t) + sigma_lam cdot sqrt(lambda(t)) dW_t
differentialEquations.interpretation: Arrival rate tracks diurnal baseline lambda_base(t) while self-exciting retry and outage jumps dN_retry and Cox-Ingersoll-Ross volatility capture surge dynamics

differentialEquations.name: Continuous Agent Shrinkage Jacobi Diffusion
differentialEquations.formula: ds_shrink(t) = theta_shr cdot (s_plan(t) - s_shrink(t)) dt + eta_fat cdot Phi_fat(t) dt + sigma_shr cdot sqrt(s_shrink(t) cdot (1 - s_shrink(t))) dB_t
differentialEquations.interpretation: Shrinkage mean-reverts toward planned schedule s_plan(t) on [0, 1] while accumulated occupancy fatigue Phi_fat(t) drives upward unplanned drift

differentialEquations.name: Occupancy Fatigue Accumulation & Staffing Control Flow
differentialEquations.formula: dPhi_fat(t) cdot dt^-1 = gamma_load cdot max(rho_occ(t) - rho_crit, 0) - mu_rec cdot (1 - rho_occ(t)), with dDelta_N(t) cdot dt^-1 = u_wfm(t) - N_sched(t) cdot (ds_shrink(t) cdot dt^-1) - dN_req(t) cdot dt^-1
differentialEquations.interpretation: Fatigue accumulates whenever occupancy rho_occ exceeds critical threshold rho_crit (~0.85) and recovers during idle intervals, coupling directly into net staffing Delta_N(t)

scaleInvariants: Square-root staffing elasticity: relative shrinkage variance decays as N_sched^-0.5 across pooled multi-skill rosters
O(1) streaming Kalman-Bucy filter update for intraday arrival intensity lambda(t) and shrinkage drift at 1-second telemetry ticks
Work-energy conservation over diurnal cycles: excess occupancy above rho_crit integrates linearly into downstream unplanned absenteeism and AHT inflation
